issue_context.title: Unexpected ambiguous error in `insert on duplicatted key `
comments:
> MySQL's behavior is too strange. I think current TiDB's behavior is more intuitive. And TiDB's is the same with PG's. I would like to mark this issue as wont-fix.

From @winoros

review_comments: Why do we need to clone the `RetType`?

This looks not right, check out this case:
In MySQL:
```
mysql> create table t2(f1 int primary key, f2 int);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> insert into t2 values(1,2),(2,1);
Query OK, 2 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Records: 2  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> INSERT INTO t2 (f1, f2) SELECT f2 f1, f1 FROM t2 src ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE f1 = 10 + src.f1;
Query OK, 4 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Records: 2  Duplicates: 2  Warnings: 0

mysql> select * from t2;
+----+------+
| f1 | f2   |
+----+------+
| 11 |    1 |
| 12 |    2 |
+----+------+
```
while in TiDB after applying your patch:
```
mysql> create table t2(f1 int primary key, f2 int);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.00 sec)

mysql> insert into t2 values(1,2),(2,1);
Query OK, 2 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Records: 2  Duplicates: 0  Warnings: 0

mysql> INSERT INTO t2 (f1, f2) SELECT f2 f1, f1 FROM t2 src ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE f1 = 10 + src.f1;
Query OK, 4 rows affected (0.00 sec)
Records: 2  Duplicates: 2  Warnings: 0

mysql> select * from t2;
+----+------+
| f1 | f2   |
+----+------+
| 11 |    2 |
| 12 |    1 |
+----+------+
```

Seems like MySQL would resolve the `src.f1` to the column which has original name `f1` in this query, not the column which has alias name `f1` while its original column name is `f2`.
Could you please help fix this as well?

```sql
INSERT INTO t2 (f1, f2)
   SELECT src.f1 f2, src.f2 f1 FROM t2 src where src.f2=1
  ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE f1 = 100 + src.f2
```
This resolver is so strange.
There are three `src.f2`, first and second are same.But the third is not.
I will try to fix it.

This change looks too ad-hoc, we are trying very hard now to remove unnecessary fields from `Column`, do we have any other solution which is more graceful to achieve the purpose of this PR? For example, add a flag parameter in `FindColumn` to indicate if "ambiguous column" error should be ignored? @winoros Any suggestion?

This is not easy to do.If two colums both come from `select` of `insert ... select...`,we can ignore the `ambiguous error` .But if one comes from `select` and another comes from `insert`. we must throw the error.
For example:
1. ` insert into t(a,b,f1) select f1,f2,f2 from t2 on duplicate key update a = f2` 
2. ` insert into t(a,b,f1) select f1,f2,f2 from t2 on duplicate key update a = f1`
The first one is ok, but second one is not.
So we must know each column if it is from `select` of `insert... select`.
